candidates_passed.name: Habitat Shifting & Alteration
candidates_passed.desc: Climate change primarily alters habitat composition, location, or physical state: sea-level rise, desertification, tundra thaw, coral bleaching, shifting biomes/ecotones.

candidates_passed.name: Droughts
candidates_passed.desc: Prolonged rainfall deficits or water scarcity outside normal variation causing ecosystem degradation or species mortality.

candidates_passed.name: Temperature Extremes
candidates_passed.desc: Heat/cold extremes outside normal variation: heat waves, cold spells, ocean temperature anomalies, glacier/sea-ice disappearance.

candidates_passed.name: Storms & Flooding
candidates_passed.desc: Extreme precipitation/wind events outside normal variation: hurricanes, cyclones, tornadoes, hail/ice storms, blizzards, associated flooding/erosion.

candidates_passed.name: Other Impacts
candidates_passed.desc: Climate/severe-weather impacts not covered above: phenological mismatch, increased variability, compound events.

candidates_passed.name: Invasive Non-Native/Alien Species/Diseases
candidates_passed.desc: Harmful non-native plants, animals, pathogens introduced intentionally or accidentally by humans AND causing negative ecological impacts on native biodiversity. Includes feral domesticated animals when effectively unmanaged. Boundary: if livestock periodically managed/rounded up as production, use Livestock Farming & Ranching. If little/no management and function as feral/invasive, use here. NEVER use for deliberate reintroductions or translocations of native species within their native range.

candidates_passed.name: Problematic Native Species/Diseases
candidates_passed.desc: Native taxa becoming unusually abundant or out-of-balance due to human-driven changes: native species outbreaks, native predators overabundant due to subsidies, native pathogens increasing due to altered conditions. Boundary: if origin clearly non-native use Invasive Non-Native/Alien Species/Diseases. If origin truly unknown use Problematic Species/Diseases of Unknown Origin.

candidates_passed.name: Introduced Genetic Material
candidates_passed.desc: Human-altered or transported genetic material affecting native populations via genetic introgression: GMO crops/insects/trees, non-local seed stock in restoration, hatchery-origin fish affecting wild gene pools. Boundary: if non-native organism becomes invasive as a species use Invasive Non-Native/Alien Species/Diseases; if emphasis is genetic mixing/stocking altering gene pools use here.

candidates_passed.name: Problematic Species/Diseases of Unknown Origin
candidates_passed.desc: Harmful taxon/pathogen where origin cannot be determined (unclear whether non-native vs native). Use only after attempting to decide between Invasive Non-Native/Alien Species/Diseases and Problematic Native Species/Diseases.

candidates_passed.name: Viral/Prion-induced Diseases
candidates_passed.desc: Disease threats where causative agent is specifically a virus or prion: West Nile Virus, Rabies, Foot-and-Mouth Disease, BSE/scrapie.

candidates_passed.name: Diseases of Unknown Cause
candidates_passed.desc: Disease syndrome described as a threat but pathogen/agent is unknown. Record disease name and symptoms. Recode once causative agent becomes known

- ACTIVE: a process described in present tense as currently occurring
- HISTORICAL: a past driver that caused the biodiversity change being studied
- IMPLICIT: a pressure inferred from the conservation or management context

- Extract non-biological resources leads to Energy Production & Mining
- Build permanent non-agricultural infrastructure leads to Residential & Commercial Development or Transportation

- Ecological process altered leads to Natural System Modifications
- Non-living substance introduced into environment leads to Pollution
- Living organism introduced or proliferating leads to Invasive & Other Problematic Species, Genes & Diseases
- Built linear infrastructure creates fragmentation or barrier effects leads to Transportation & Service Corridors
- Non-consumptive human presence causes disturbance leads to Human Intrusions & Disturbance

3. AGENT TYPE: What is the threat agent? For example only:
- A living organism leads to Invasive & Other Problematic Species, Genes & Diseases
- A non-living substance leads to Pollution
- A built structure with compact footprint leads to Residential & Commercial Development
- A linear corridor or utility line leads to Transportation & Service Corridors
- A human activity without permanent footprint leads to Human Intrusions & Disturbance

- ACTIVE: a process described in present tense as currently occurring
- HISTORICAL: a past driver that caused the biodiversity change being studied
- IMPLICIT: a pressure inferred from the conservation or management context

Do not require explicit threat terminology. Infer from ecological and conservation context.

- Extract non-biological resources leads to Energy Production & Mining
- Build permanent non-agricultural infrastructure leads to Residential & Commercial Development or Transportation

- Organisms removed from the system leads to Biological Resource Use
- Habitat converted to another land use leads to Agriculture & Aquaculture or Residential & Commercial Development
- Ecological process altered leads to Natural System Modifications
- Non-living substance introduced into environment leads to Pollution
- Living organism introduced or proliferating leads to Invasive & Other Problematic Species, Genes & Diseases
- Built linear infrastructure creates fragmentation or barrier effects leads to Transportation & Service Corridors
- Non-consumptive human presence causes disturbance leads to Human Intrusions & Disturbance

- A living organism leads to Invasive & Other Problematic Species, Genes & Diseases
- A non-living substance leads to Pollution
- A built structure with compact footprint leads to Residential & Commercial Development
